newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul shares end lower despite blue chip buying.
newsitem.headline: Seoul shares end lower despite blue chip buying.

text.p: Buying in large cap and blue chip shares was not enough to drag the Seoul stock market higher, which closed lower for the sixth consecutive session on Wednesday.
The composite stock index provisionally ended down 1.96 points to 661.39. Declining shares overwhelmed advancers 672 to 267 with 87 unchanged. Volume was a relatively active 31.5 million shares.
"There is nothing new in the market and most institutional investors have decided to simply wait and see what next year brings," said a Dongsuh Securities broker.
Brokers said that blue chips were boosted by talk that the finance ministry had asked pension funds to buy 300 billion won worth of shares by the end of the year.
POSCO climbed 1,500 won higher to 37,200, and Hyundai Motor gained 600 won to 19,800. KEPCO, which was unchanged at 25,000, saw foreign buying interest.
Samsung Electronics ended 800 won higher at 46,000.
Sammi Steel, which said it planned to sell off parts of its stainless steel business to POSCO, finished at its upper limit of 3,690, 270 won higher.
Selling was focused on small and mid-cap shares.
"Usually at the end of the year, institutions buy to boost their portfolios," said one local fund manager. "This year, we're selling to reduce our losses."
